speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're in a lot of pain. Can you describe exactly where the pain is located in your right groin and whether you can move your right leg at all?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: I observe that your right leg appears shortened and externally rotated. Can you confirm if you are experiencing any numbness or tingling in your right foot or toes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positioning of your leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is classic for a posterior hip dislocation, which often occurs in rear-end collisions when the knee strikes the dashboard. I need to rule out an associated fracture or soft tissue damage, so I will order imaging immediately. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms a posterior hip dislocation without fracture. I will now request medical images to review the dislocation further. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms a posterior hip dislocation, which is a surgical emergency. I will now proceed with immediate closed reduction of the hip to prevent avascular necrosis of the femoral head. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation
